newsitem.title: USA: NYCE launches potato futures, 200 lots traded.
newsitem.headline: NYCE launches potato futures, 200 lots traded.

text.p: Potato industry professionals got a boost today when the New York Cotton Exchange (NYCE) launched its new potato futures contract.
"This is a real price discovery tool for almost everyone who eats or uses potatoes," said George Gero, chairman of the NYCE's newly-created SPUD Division.

He said the $2.3 billion-a-year industry has been in need for such a tool for the past two years as weather and firm export business has led to extreme price fluctuations. A price run-up in 1994 prompted growers to plant large amounts of potatoes in 1995, which resulted in plummeting prices in 1996.
"No one had a chance to manage risk," Gero said. "The grower couldn't hedge, the shipper couldn't hedge and those who over-contracted long lost money."
Today's estimated volume for potato futures, which began trading at 0945 EDT, was 200 lots. Potato options will begin trading October 1.
Delivery for the contract requires a two-to-one mixture of non-size "A" potatoes packed in 10-lb mesh bags, and 70- or 80-count carton-size potatoes packed in 50-lb cartons.

The mixture allows growers to hedge a greater portion of the value of their crop, typically composed of two-thirds "tens," or smaller potatoes in ten-lb bags, and one-third large or Russet potatoes, Gero said.

Price differentials for the contract are fixed, and the eight delivery points include Texas, New Mexico, Idaho, Washington, Colorado, Maine, Wisconsin and Oregon. The contract months are November, January, March, May, July and September.
Each contract calls for 85,000 pounds of U.S. Russet Burbank potatoes, the most widely-consumed potato according to industry sources.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approved the new futures contract Sept 5.
